overview: Well, it's finally here — the 2025 Preach Fantasy Playoffs kick off today, and with that comes predictions for each first-round matchup. Before getting into predictions, a look back at some league history: the league has yet to have a repeat champion in its first 5 seasons, but that very well may change this season — every champion from 2020 to 2024 has officially made the 2025 playoffs, so there's definitely a good chance. There are also a couple of playoff rematches this round: Ryan and Ethan face off in Round 1 for the third time (also met in '20 and '23), and Cole and Anthony meet in Round 1 for a second time (also met in '20).

matchups.blurb: The first matchup of the 2025 Preach Fantasy Playoffs is between the 1st and 8th seeds, and honestly this might be a tighter matchup than we've seen from prior years' 1v8. Since 2022, the 1v8 matchup has been decided by about 41 points on average, so A$AP should have the upper hand here. However, WoaW has averaged about 124 points per game the last three weeks while A$AP averaged 113 in the same period. My verdict: give me A$AP to advance.

We witnessed a top-4 season from a PF/G perspective, and it would be a shame if that dominance ended early, but I do think RWB has a shot here in Round 1. The stats may not show it, but STD has had two sub-90 performances in the past 5 weeks, while RWB has stayed about that mark all season. It may be unlikely, but there's a chance the 7th seed knocks out the 2nd seed. My verdict: although I like RWB's chances, I still think STD will get the job done and advance.

The final matchup of the 1st round, and with that comes the biggest difference in projections between the two teams. However, MFGA has looked very beatable the past 6 weeks, averaging around 94 points per game in that period, which makes this matchup very intriguing. Still, Cooking's success will largely rely on Michael Wilson, and with the Houston matchup I don't see the magic continuing. My verdict: despite MFGA's recent poor play, I think they'll do just enough to move on.

In theory the 4v5 matchup should be the closest one in the first round, but I really don't think that'll be the case this year. LP started the season strong, going 6-2 in the first 8 weeks, but then injuries came along and they haven't left. On the other hand, Grits has gone 4-2 in the past 6 weeks with two monster performances in Weeks 13 and 14. My verdict: I think the hot hand gets the win in Round 1, so give me Grits to move on.
